newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland's Niinisto sees lower '97 unemployment.
newsitem.headline: Finland's Niinisto sees lower '97 unemployment.

text.p: Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Tuesday Finnish unemployment next year was likely to be lower than forecast by the ministry, but he also said state spending would be cut further if growth remained below forecast.

He said that strong expectations of growth made it fair to expect the 1997 unemployment rate -- projected at 15.4 percent, down one percentage point on this year -- "to actually be even slightly better than forecast."

"The view of Finnish economists is now more uniform than for a long, long time ... Everybody is expecting a better tomorrow, strong economic growth," Niinisto told the representatives' meeting of the Central Union of Agricultural Producers (MTK).
"It really looks like ... four percent GDP growth next year is within reach," Niinisto said.
The ministry's forecast for 1997 GDP growth is 3.9 percent, up from 2.8 percent this year.

Already agreed 1997 state budget expenditure cuts "will not be enough unless the economy develops in line with forecasts," he said, referring both to the pace of growth and to the projected fall in the rate of unemployment.
After his speech, Niinisto told reporters that by this he did "not at at all" want to signal that economic growth might not be on track.
"On the contrary, It seems that there is finally confidence in the finance ministry's figures," he said.
The ministry's 3.9 percent 1997 GDP growth forecast is slightly higher than forecasts by major independent research institutes and banks.
